title: Dependability Fastpath 45-Day Experiment Playlist
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, time-boxed runbook for a 45-day cross-functional effort to validate a repeatable way of shipping and operationalizing SLO-backed reliability improvements for model-serving features (streaming, batching hotspots, cold-cache degradation). The goal is to produce a tested template and 3 concrete artifacts: a defensible SLO definition for one target surface, an experiment that improves error/latency by >=20% under a realistic traffic slice, and a handoff package for product teams (metrics, alert rules, rollback criteria).

Why a 45-day fastpath?
- Short enough to keep momentum and minimize long planning cycles.
- Long enough to iterate on measurement, a corrective action, and an on-call verification.
- Forces pragmatic choices for cross-team scope and dependency management.

Scope (what's in/out)
In scope:
- One production model-serving route (identify below) and its downstream cache/KV interactions.
- End-to-end SLI definition (p99 latency, 5xx rate, model failure signals) and baseline collection.
- Two mitigation experiments (one config/ops change + one code change or model fallback).
- Observability enhancements needed to validate impact.
Out of scope:
- Global platform revamps (big infra projects).
- Customer contract changes or SLA negotiation.

Hypotheses (what we'll test)
H1: Adding a short-circuit fallback to a smaller, quantized model variant during KV-miss spikes can reduce 95th- and 99th-percentile latency by >=20% with <10% increase in mild semantic drift for user-facing prompts.
H2: Activating prefix-KV caching with an improved eviction policy will reduce token-level cost on the critical route by >=15% and reduce tail latency during burst patterns.
H3: A targeted synthetic traffic test plus an on-call drill will reduce incident-to-fix time for related issues by 30% after rollout.

Success metrics (binary + numeric)
- Baseline p99 latency and p95 latency collected for 2 weeks pre-experiment.
- Primary success: p99 latency improvement >=20% on the target slice OR 50% reduction in 5xx spikes during burst windows.
- Secondary: token cost/unit reduction >=10% (observed on dedicated metrics) and no customer-visible regression reported in next 7 days post-rollout.
- Operational: runbook completeness score >= 7/10 (self-eval) and playbook handed off to product and SRE.

High-level 45-day schedule (weeks)
Week 0: Kickoff + discovery (3 days)
- Identify target route (candidate: streaming-completions v2 route) and gather stakeholders (Product owner, Serving runtime, Platform infra, Observability, Solutions Eng).
- Quick audit: current SLIs, dashboards, alerts, runbook fragments.
- Decide canary policy and rollback thresholds.
Week 1-2: Measurement baseline + small telemetry gaps (14 days)
- Instrument missing signals (model-fallback counter, KV-miss histogram, request-size tag).
- Run synthetic traffic to validate telemetry and label production traces for the target slice.
- Draft SLO proposal and get 1:1 feedback from product.
Week 3: Experiment engineering (7 days)
- Implement fallback switch (config + feature flag) and KV eviction tweak behind flags.
- Create automated canary job for the two mitigations.
Week 4: Canary + iteration (7 days)
- Run canary at 1% then 10% traffic windows during low-impact hours.
- Runbook test: simulate a cache outage and validate on-call playbook.
Week 5-6: Rollout + handoff (10 days)
- Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% if metrics OK.
- Prepare Handoff doc: SLO definition, dashboards, alert thresholds, rollback steps, ticket templates.
- Post-mortem & short retro; create acceptance ticket for product.

Roles & RACI (proposed)
- Program lead (Aisha Patel) — overall drive, timeline, stakeholder updates.
- SRE lead (Evan Morales) — telemetry, runbook, on-call drill owner.
- Serving runtime engineer (Marcus Kline) — implements fallback and performance tune.
- Observability (Lena Zhao) — dashboards, traces, synthetic jobs.
- Product owner (Priya Singh) — SLO acceptability, customer risk sign-off.
- Solutions Eng (Diego Alvarez) — customer impact assessment and rollout communications.
RACI quick mapping:
- SLO definition: Responsible=SRE lead, Accountable=Product owner, Consulted=Observability, Informed=Program lead.
- Canary rollout: Responsible=Serving runtime, Accountable=Program lead, Consulted=SRE, Informed=Solutions Eng.

Cross-team dependencies and blockers (top risks)
- Missing model-variant that is compatible with semantic fallback. Mitigation: pre-check available model artifacts, if none, pivot to controlled throttling policy.
- Observability gaps (no model-fallback counter). Mitigation: reserve 2 days in Week1 for quick instrumentation and synthetic verification.
- Capacity constraints on Dedicated clusters for canary traffic. Mitigation: request a small reservation (1 GPU equivalent) and use traffic shaping.

Communication plan
- Kickoff doc in Confluence + short summary in #ops-dependability.
- Weekly 30-min sync with stakeholders (Mon 11am PT).
- Daily stand in Weeks 2–4 via short triage thread in Slack (ops-dependability).
- Postmortem and 15-minute executive TL;DR for product leadership.

Experiment templates (copy/paste)
- Title: [Experiment] short-circuit-fallback-v1
- Goal: reduce p99 latency on route X by 20%
- Audience: internal, product approval required
- Preconditions: model-variant v2 available in artifact store; metric 'model.fallback.count' instrumented
- Test steps: enable flag at 1% for 1h; monitor p95/p99, 5xx, semantic-eval-samples; if any safety triggers, rollback immediately.
- Exit criteria: metric attainment OR safety trigger.

Runbook handoff checklist (minimum)
- Defined SLO document with objective and indicator definitions (p99 latency, error budget burn calc).
- Dashboard links and graph time windows.
- Alert rules: paging threshold and warning threshold (both numeric).
- Rollback play steps and who to page.
- Post-rollout observation window: 7 days with weekly checks.

Quick templates: ticket names and tags
- JIRA: SRE-EXPERIMENT-[shortname] e.g., SRE-EXPERIMENT-fallback-01
- Slack tags: #ops-dependability #canary-updates

Budget and resourcing notes
- Estimate: 6 engineer-weeks across teams (split: SRE 1.5w, serving 2w, observability 1w, program lead 1w, solutions eng 0.5w).
- Contingency: reserve an additional 1w for unexpected telemetry work.

Risks & mitigations (table-style notes)
- Risk: customer-visible semantic regression. Mitigation: sample-based semantic checks, rollback threshold at 2x baseline degradation on selected prompts.
- Risk: false-positive telemetry flaps. Mitigation: smoothing windows and manual review by Observability before Pager escalation.

Open questions / Notes to self
- Which production route best represents customer impact but is sufficiently isolated to test? Candidate list: streaming-completions-v2, chat-streaming-low-latency. Need product to pick by kickoff.
- Do we have an accepted lightweight semantic-eval harness for quick checks? If not, Solutions Eng to prototype one.
- Does the Dedicated pool policy allow a 1-GPU short reservation without bumping other teams? Platform to confirm (infra-ticket pending).

Next steps (immediate)
- Create Confluence kickoff doc and link to this draft (Aisha) — today.
- Product chooses target route and signs SLO proposal by Day+3 (Priya).
- Observability creates synthetic job templates and flags missing metrics by Day+5 (Lena).

Appendix: quick links and references
- Confluence draft (placeholder): https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/display/SRE/Dependability+Fastpath+45d
- Example incident postmortem template: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=28923
- Example SLO calc spreadsheet (linked): https://sheets.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-example

-- End draft --

Comments: keep this intentionally pragmatic and focused on a single surface. The objective is reusable artifacts, not a complete platform rewrite. Use the experiment templates as the canonical way to run future 30–60 day reliability sprints.
